title: Bekhorot 12
description: With what a firstborn donkey may and may not be redeemed: the animals the mishna excludes and the dilemmas that follow, the priest who is handed an unredeemed donkey, who bears the loss when the lamb or the donkey dies, and when the redemption should take place.
topics: 🐑 A calf, a gazelle, a slaughtered animal, a hybrid, a koy: what is not a “lamb” for redeeming a donkey
🔁 Ben Bag Bag’s “lamb, lamb” from the Paschal offering, and “you shall redeem, you shall redeem”
❓ Dilemmas: a ben pekua, a lamb that looks like a goat, disqualified consecrated animals, an animal bought with Sabbatical produce
🔥 Rav Ḥisda: “for consumption,” not for burning, and why ḥalla is different
🧑‍⚖️ Priests are suspect about firstborn donkeys: redeem it in front of the owner
⚰️ The lamb died, or the donkey died: Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis on who bears the loss
📅 Redeem immediately, or after thirty days?

a1.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין פּוֹדִין לֹא בְּעֵגֶל וְלֹא בְּחַיָּה, לֹא בִּשְׁחוּטָה וְלֹא בִּטְרֵיפָה, וְלֹא בְּכִלְאַיִם וְלֹא בְּכוֹי. וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מַתִּיר בַּכִּלְאַיִם מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא שֶׂה, וְאוֹסֵר בַּכּוֹי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא סָפֵק. נְתָנוֹ לְכֹהֵן — אֵין הַכֹּהֵן רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּפְרִישׁ שֶׂה תַּחְתָּיו.

a2.he: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי? בֶּן בַּג בַּג הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: בֶּן בַּג בַּג אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״שֶׂה״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״שֶׂה״, מָה לְּהַלָּן פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ, אַף כָּאן פְּרָט לְכׇל הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַלָּלוּ.

a3.he: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה, אַף כָּאן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״תִּפְדֶּה״ ״תִּפְדֶּה״ — רִיבָּה.

a4.he: אִי ״תִּפְדֶּה״ ״תִּפְדֶּה״ רִיבָּה, אֲפִילּוּ כֹּל הָנֵי נָמֵי? אִם כֵּן, ״שֶׂה״ ״שֶׂה״ מַאי אַהֲנִי לֵיהּ?

a5.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִפְדּוֹת בְּבֶן פְּקוּעָה? אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, דְּכֵיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: בֶּן פְּקוּעָה טָעוּן שְׁחִיטָה, שֶׂה מְעַלְּיָא הוּא. אֶלָּא כִּי תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן, דְּאָמְרִי: שְׁחִיטַת אִמּוֹ מְטַהַרְתּוֹ.

a6.he: כְּבִישְׂרָא בְּדִיקּוּלָא דָּמֵי, אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּהַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא רָהֵיט וְאָזֵיל, ״שֶׂה״ קָרֵינָא בֵּיהּ?

a7.he: מָר זוּטְרָא אָמַר: אֵין פּוֹדִין, וְרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: פּוֹדִין.

a8.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְמָר זוּטְרָא: מַאי דַּעְתָּיךְ? דְּיָלְפַתְּ מִפֶּסַח. אִי מָה לְהַלָּן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה, אַף כָּאן זָכָר תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה! ״תִּפְדֶּה״ ״תִּפְדֶּה״ — רִיבָּה.

a9.he: אִי ״תִּפְדֶּה״ ״תִּפְדֶּה״ רִיבָּה, אֲפִילּוּ בֶּן פְּקוּעָה נָמֵי! אִם כֵּן, ״שֶׂה״ ״שֶׂה״ מַאי אַהֲנִי לֵיהּ?

a10.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִפְדּוֹת בְּנִדְמָה? אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, הַשְׁתָּא בְּכִלְאַיִם פָּרְקִינַן, בְּנִדְמָה מִיבַּעְיָא?

a11.he: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן, בְּכִלְאַיִם הוּא דְּלָא פָּרְקִינַן, בְּנִדְמָה פָּרְקִינַן, אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא שְׁנָא?

a12.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: פָּרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז — אֵין פּוֹדִין, הָא רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז — פּוֹדִין. מַנִּי? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר — הָא בְּכִלְאַיִם נָמֵי פָּרְקִינַן! אֶלָּא לָאו רַבָּנַן הִיא?

a13.he: לָא, לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא, גּוּפַהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּפָרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז — אֵין פּוֹדִין. לָא תֵּימָא: זִיל אַבָּתְרֵיהּ דִּידֵיהּ, וְהַאי עֵז מְעַלְּיָא הוּא, אֶלָּא זִיל בָּתַר אִימֵּיהּ — וְהַאי עֵגֶל הוּא.

a14.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵיזֶהוּ כִּלְאַיִם? רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז, וְאָבִיו שֶׂה. אָבִיו שֶׂה, כִּלְאַיִם הוּא? נִדְמֶה הוּא! אֶלָּא, אֵיזֶהוּ דָּמֵי לְכִלְאַיִם, דְּשַׁוְּיוּהּ רַבָּנַן כִּי כִלְאַיִם? רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז, וְאָבִיו שֶׂה.

a15.he: לְמַאי? אִי לְקָדָשִׁים — מֵהֵיכָא דִּמְמַעֵט כִּלְאַיִם, מֵהָתָם מְמַעֵט נִדְמֶה, דְּתַנְיָא: ״שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב״ — פְּרָט לְכִלְאַיִם, ״אוֹ עֵז״ — פְּרָט לְנִדְמֶה!

a16.he: אִי לִבְכוֹר, ״אַךְ בְּכוֹר שׁוֹר״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר!

a17.he: אֶלָּא לְמַעֲשֵׂר, ״תַּחַת״ ״תַּחַת״ מִקֳּדָשִׁים גָּמַר! אֶלָּא לְפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר.

a18.he: לָא, לְעוֹלָם לְמַעֲשֵׂר, וּכְגוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין, מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא ״הַעֲבָרָה״ ״הַעֲבָרָה״ מִבְּכוֹר גָּמַר,

a20.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִפְדּוֹת בִּפְסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין?

a21.he: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה — חוּלִּין הוּא, כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה.

a22.he: מַאי? כֵּיוָן דְּאָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה, אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר?

a23.he: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא תָּפֵיס פִּדְיוֹנוֹ, אַפְקוֹעֵי אִיסּוּרָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא?

a24.he: אָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא: מִי זוּטַר מַאי דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ, ״כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל״? מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל אֵין פּוֹדִין, אַף פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין אֵין פּוֹדִין!

b1.he: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נָמֵי, ״צְבִי וְאַיָּל״ כְּתִיב בְּהוּ.

b2.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לִפְדּוֹת בְּבֶהֱמַת שְׁבִיעִית?

b3.he: וַדַּאי — לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, לַאֲכִילָה אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא לִסְחוֹרָה. כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ — סָפֵק.

b4.he: וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ סָפֵק, כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

b5.he: מַאי כֵּיוָן דְּמַפְרֵישׁ טָלֶה וְהוּא לְעַצְמוֹ, ״לְאׇכְלָה״ קָרֵינָא בֵּיהּ, אוֹ דִילְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּכַמָּה דְּלָא מַפְקַע אִיסּוּרֵיהּ לָא מִישְׁתְּרֵי, כִּסְחוֹרָה דָּמֵי?

b6.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בֶּהֱמַת שְׁבִיעִית אֵין פּוֹדִין בָּהּ אֶת הַוַּדַּאי, אֲבָל פּוֹדִין בָּהּ אֶת הַסָּפֵק.

b7.he: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בֶּהֱמַת שְׁבִיעִית פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה, וְחַיֶּיבֶת בַּמַּתָּנוֹת.

b8.he: פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה — ״לְאׇכְלָה״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא לִשְׂרֵיפָה, וְחַיֶּיבֶת בַּמַּתָּנוֹת — דִּ״לְאָכְלָה״ קָרֵינָא בַּהּ.

b9.he: מֵיתִיבִי: הָאוֹכֵל מֵעִיסַּת שְׁבִיעִית עַד שֶׁלֹּא הוּרְמָה חַלָּתָהּ — חַיָּיב מִיתָה.

b10.he: וְאַמַּאי? כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ מִטַּמְּיָא בַּת שְׂרֵיפָה הִיא, ״לְאׇכְלָה״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, וְלֹא לִשְׂרֵיפָה!

b12.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: מִנַּיִן לָאוֹכֵל מֵעִיסַּת שְׁבִיעִית עַד שֶׁלֹּא הוּרְמָה חַלָּתָהּ שֶׁחַיָּיב מִיתָה — שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם״.

b13.he: וְלִגְמַר מִינַּהּ! הָתָם עִיקָּר לַאֲכִילָה, הָכָא עִיקָּר לִשְׂרֵיפָה.

b14.he: נְתָנוֹ לְכֹהֵן כּוּ׳. תְּנֵינָא לְהָא דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ, וְאָמַר לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן: ״תְּנֵהוּ לִי וַאֲנִי אֶפְדֵּהוּ״ — הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִתְּנוּ לוֹ, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן פְּדָאוֹ בְּפָנָיו.

b15.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת נֶחְשְׁדוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים עַל פִּטְרֵי חֲמוֹרִים. פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּמַחְזַק לַן דְּמִיקְּרֵי, אֲבָל בִּסְתָמָא לָא — קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּמוֹרֵה בַּהּ הֶיתֵּירָא.

b16.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּפְרִישׁ פִּדְיוֹן פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר וָמֵת, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: חַיָּיבִין בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ, כַּחֲמֵשׁ סְלָעִים שֶׁל בֵּן, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין חַיָּיבִין בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ, כְּפִדְיוֹן מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי.

b17.he: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי צָדוֹק עַל פִּדְיוֹן פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר שֶׁמֵּת, שֶׁאֵין כָּאן לַכֹּהֵן כְּלוּם. מֵת פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יִקָּבֵר, וּמוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָתוֹ שֶׁל טָלֶה. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהִקָּבֵר, וְטָלֶה לַכֹּהֵן.

b18.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? דִּכְתִיב: ״אַךְ פָּדֹה תִפְדֶּה וְגוֹ׳״, מָה בְּכוֹר אָדָם חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ, אַף בְּכוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה חַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ.

b19.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי מָה בְּכוֹר אָדָם מוּתָּר בַּהֲנָאָה, אַף בְּכוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מוּתָּר! וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָתְנַן: מֵת פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יִקָּבֵר. מַאי יִקָּבֵר? לָאו דְּאָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה?

b20.he: לָא, יִקָּבֵר כִּבְכוֹר אָדָם. אֶלָּא, אָדָם בְּכוֹר הוּא דְּבָעֵי קְבוּרָה, פָּשׁוּט לָא בָּעֵי קְבוּרָה?

b21.he: וְעוֹד תַּנְיָא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ סְפֵק פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ — שֶׁמַּפְרִישׁ טָלֶה עָלָיו, וְהוּא שֶׁלּוֹ!

b22.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא ״אַךְ פָּדֹה תִפְדֶּה״, לִפְדִיָּיה הִקַּשְׁיתִּיו, וְלֹא לְדָבָר אַחֵר.

b23.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: הָעֲרָכִין — בִּשְׁעָתָן, וּפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן — אַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, פִּדְיוֹן פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר — לְאַלְתַּר.

b24.he: וּפִדְיוֹן פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר לְאַלְתַּר? וּרְמִינְהִי: אֵין בַּעֲרָכִין, וּבְפִדְיוֹן הַבֵּן, וּבִנְזִירוּת, וּבְפֶטֶר חֲמוֹר — פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשִׁים.

b26.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לוֹמַר שֶׁאִם פְּדָאוֹ — פָּדוּי, מִכְּלָל דִּבְנוֹ אִם פְּדָאוֹ אֵינוֹ פָּדוּי? וְהָאִיתְּמַר: הַפּוֹדֶה אֶת בְּנוֹ בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, רַב אָמַר: בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי!

b27.he: לָאו אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רָבָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא ״מֵעַכְשָׁיו״ — אֵין בְּנוֹ פָּדוּי.

messages.text: Mishna

One may not redeem a firstborn donkey, neither with a calf, nor with an undomesticated animal, nor with a slaughtered animal, nor with a tereifa, nor with a hybrid of a sheep and a goat, nor with a koy, which is an animal with regard to which it is uncertain whether it is domesticated or undomesticated.

notes.he: צבי ואיל:
notes.en: Mishna. Nor with an undomesticated animal: a gazelle or a hart.

notes.he: ואפי' שה שחוט:
notes.en: Nor with a slaughtered animal: even a slaughtered lamb.

notes.he: שנחתכו רגליה מן הארכובה ולמעלה:
notes.en: A tereifa: whose legs were cut off from the knee joint and above.

notes.he: תייש הבא על הרחל:
notes.en: A hybrid: a billy goat that mated with a ewe.

notes.he: ספק חיה ספק בהמה:
notes.en: A koy: it is uncertain whether it is an undomesticated animal or a domesticated animal.

notes.he: כגון שנחתכו רגליו מן הארכובה ולמעלה:
notes.en: Nor with a tereifa: for example, one whose legs were cut off from the knee joint and above.

notes.he: בשה הבא מעז ומרחל:
notes.en: Nor with a hybrid: with a lamb that comes from a goat and a ewe.

notes.he: הבא מן התיש ומן הצביה:
notes.en: Nor with a koy: which comes from a billy goat and a female gazelle.

messages.text: And Rabbi Eliezer deems it permitted to redeem a firstborn donkey with a hybrid of a sheep and a goat, because it is a lamb, i.e., that hybrid has the status of a lamb, but prohibits redeeming it with a koy, because its status is uncertain.

notes.he: דבין רחל ובין עז קרויין שה:
notes.en: Because it is a lamb: since both a ewe and a goat are called seh [a lamb].

notes.he: ר' אלעזר גרסינן ולא גרסינן רבי אליעזר וכן מוכח במרובה (ב"ק דף עח.) דאמר ר' אלעזר דמתיר בכלאים מפני שהוא שה דאינו אלא להוציא כלאים למאי הלכתא ומשני לטמא שנולד מן הטהור ועיבורו מן הטמא ודלא כר' יהושע דאי כר' יהושע משה כבשים ושה עזים נפקא וכל שכן דלא כר' אליעזר דשרי לעיל בפירקין אלמא דרבי אליעזר פליג על רבי אלעזר ור' אליעזר בר פלוגתיה דרבי יהושע:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer permits with a hybrid: we read “Rabbi Elazar,” and we do not read “Rabbi Eliezer.” And so it is proven in the chapter Merubba (Bava Kamma 78a), where it says that according to Rabbi Elazar, who permits with a hybrid because it is a lamb, [the verse] serves only to exclude a hybrid; for what halakha? And it answers: for a non-kosher animal born from a kosher one, whose conception was from a non-kosher one. And [that is] not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua, since according to Rabbi Yehoshua that is derived from “a lamb of the sheep and a lamb of the goats,” and all the more so not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who permits [such an animal] earlier in our chapter. Evidently Rabbi Eliezer disagrees with Rabbi Elazar, and it is Rabbi Eliezer who disputes with Rabbi Yehoshua.

notes.dh: ור' אלעזר מתיר בכלאים מפני שהוא שה
notes.he: שאביו ואמו מין בהמה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Elazar permits with a hybrid because it is a lamb: since its father and mother are both a species of domesticated animal. [Rabbeinu Gershom reads Rabbi Elazar where the daf reads Rabbi Eliezer.]

messages.text: If one gave the firstborn donkey to a priest, the priest may not keep it unless he first designates a lamb in its stead for redemption.

notes.he: הפטר חמור:
notes.en: If one gave it to a priest: the firstborn donkey.

notes.he: הפטר חמור:
notes.en: If one gave it to a priest: the firstborn donkey.

notes.he: שלא יערפנו עד שיפריש הכהן שה תחתיו והוא שלו מפני גזרת הכתוב ואם לא תפדה וערפתו:
notes.en: The priest may not keep it: [meaning] he should not break its neck until the priest designates a lamb in its stead, and it is his, because of the decree of the verse: “And if you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck.”

messages.text: The daf’s text reads Rabbi Eliezer in this mishna and in the Gemara that follows. Tosafot and Rabbeinu Gershom read Rabbi Elazar.
Gemara
Whose opinion is expressed in the first clause of the mishna? It is the opinion of ben Bag Bag, as it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: One may not redeem a firstborn donkey, neither with a calf, nor with an undomesticated animal

messages.text: It is stated here, with regard to the redemption of a firstborn donkey: “And you shall redeem a firstborn donkey with a lamb” (Exodus 13:13), and it is stated there, with regard to the Paschal offering: “In the tenth day of this month they shall take to them every man a lamb” (Exodus 12:3).

verse.he: וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר חֲמֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה וְאִם־לֹא תִפְדֶּה וַעֲרַפְתּוֹ וְכֹל בְּכוֹר אָדָם בְּבָנֶיךָ תִּפְדֶּה׃
verse.en: But every firstling donkey you shall redeem with a sheep; if you do not redeem it, you must break its neck. And you must redeem every male first-born among your children.

notes.he: בפסח:
notes.en: Gemara. There: with regard to the Paschal offering.

notes.he: תפדה בשה ונאמר להלן בפסח שה תמים זכר בן שנה:
notes.en: It is stated here “lamb”: “you shall redeem with a lamb”; and it is stated there, with regard to the Paschal offering, “a lamb… unblemished, a male, in its first year.”

messages.text: By inference, just as there, with regard to the Paschal offering, the Torah excludes all of these names, i.e., all of these types of animals listed in the mishna, from being fit for sacrifice as a Paschal offering, so too here, with regard to the redemption of a firstborn donkey, the Torah excludes all of these names.

notes.he: שבמשנתנו. הפסח אינו בא עגל וחיה דכתיב (שמות יב) שה מן הכבשים ומן העזים ולא שחוט דבעינן שחיטה לשם פסח וכלאים נמי לא דכלאים אין קריבין לגבי מזבח כדקתני לקמן שור וכשב פרט לכלאים:
notes.en: All of these names: those in our mishna. The Paschal offering does not come from a calf or from an undomesticated animal, as it is written: “From the sheep or from the goats” (Exodus 12:5); nor from a slaughtered animal, since we require slaughter for the sake of the Paschal offering; and not from a hybrid either, since hybrids are not offered on the altar, as is taught below: “A bull or a sheep” excludes a hybrid.

notes.dh: מה להלן פרט לכל השמות הללו
notes.he: משום דפסח קדשים הוא ואמרינן גבי קדשים שור או כשב (לרבות) פרט לכלאים או עז פרט לנדמה כי יולד פרט ליוצא דופן:
notes.en: Just as there it excludes all of these names: because the Paschal offering is a sacrificial animal, and we say with regard to sacrificial animals: “A bull or a sheep” excludes a hybrid, “or a goat” excludes one that resembles another species, “when it is born” excludes one born by caesarean section.

notes.he: בהאי תפדה בשה פרט לכל השמות הללו:
notes.en: So too here: in this “you shall redeem with a lamb,” it excludes all of these names.

messages.text: If this halakha is derived from the Paschal offering, then perhaps just as there, the Paschal offering must be a lamb that is male, unblemished, and in its first year (Exodus 12:5), so too here, the lamb must be male, unblemished, and in its first year.

The verse states: “You shall redeem” (Exodus 13:13), and: “You shall redeem” (Exodus 34:20). This repetition serves to include female lambs, blemished lambs, and lambs that are beyond their first year.
If the repetition of the terms “you shall redeem,” “you shall redeem,” serves to include, then even all of these types of animals that are listed in the mishna should be included.
If so, what purpose does the verbal analogy of “lamb,” “lamb,” between the firstborn donkey and the Paschal offering serve?
What is the halakha with regard to redeeming a firstborn donkey with a lamb that was removed alive from its mother’s womb after the mother was ritually slaughtered [ben pekua]?
messages.lead: § A dilemma was raised before the Sages:

notes.he: שנמצא חי בבהמה שחוטה: פלוגתא דר"מ ורבנן בפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עד.):
notes.en: A ben pekua: one found alive inside a slaughtered animal. The dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis is in the chapter Behema HaMaksha (Ḥullin 74a).

notes.he: שה חי שנמצא בבטן בהמה שחוטה:
notes.en: A ben pekua: a live lamb that is found in the belly of a slaughtered animal.

messages.text: According to the opinion of Rabbi Meir you should not raise the dilemma, as since Rabbi Meir says that a ben pekua requires ritual slaughter, it is considered a full-fledged lamb. Rather, you should raise the dilemma according to the opinion of the Rabbis, who say that the slaughter of its mother renders the fetus permitted for consumption, as it is considered part of the mother, which was already slaughtered.

Is it considered like meat that is placed in a pot, i.e., as if it had been slaughtered, in which case it is included in the prohibition against redeeming a firstborn donkey with a slaughtered animal? Or perhaps since now, in any event, it runs along, we call it a lamb.

notes.he: קלחת. כלומר כשחוטה דמי ואין פודין בשחוטה:
notes.en: In a pot [bedikula]: a cauldron. That is, it is like a slaughtered animal, and one does not redeem with a slaughtered animal.

notes.he: וכל הנך אין פודין דאמר במתניתין שלא בשויין קאמרינן דאי בשויין אפי' בשלקי שרי:
notes.en: Or perhaps etc.: and all of these with which, as the mishna says, one may not redeem, we are speaking of where they are not equal in value [to the donkey]; for if they are equal in value, even [redeeming] with boiled vegetables is permitted.

notes.he: וכשחוט הוא ואין פודין בו:
notes.en: It is like meat in a pot: and it is like a slaughtered animal, and one does not redeem with it.

messages.text: One may not redeem a firstborn donkey with a ben pekua.
messages.lead: The Gemara cites a dispute with regard to this issue:

messages.text: One may redeem with it.

@Mar Zutra What is the reason for your opinion? Is it because you derive the halakhot of redeeming a firstborn donkey from the Paschal offering, and a ben pekua is unfit for sacrifice as a Paschal offering? If so, just as there, with regard to the Paschal offering, it must be male, unblemished, and in its first year, so too here, the lamb must be male, unblemished, and in its first year.

notes.he: בן פקועה פסול לפסח דאינו קרב למזבח דתניא בפ' שני דשחיטת חולין (דף לח:) כי יולד פרט ליוצא דופן:
notes.en: A ben pekua is unfit for the Paschal offering, since it is not offered on the altar, as is taught in the second chapter of Shechitat Ḥullin (38b): “When it is born” excludes one born by caesarean section.

notes.he: דילפת שה שה מפסח ובפסח אמרינן פרט ליוצא דופן והיינו בן פקועה ומשום הכי אין פודין. אי מה להלן זכר כו':
notes.en: For you derive “lamb,” “lamb” from the Paschal offering, and with regard to the Paschal offering we say: excluding one born by caesarean section, which is a ben pekua; and therefore one does not redeem [with it]. If so, just as there it must be a male etc.

messages.text: The repetition of the terms “you shall redeem,” “you shall redeem,” included a lamb that is not male, unblemished, or in its first year.
If the repetition of the terms “you shall redeem,” “you shall redeem,” included additional types of lambs, even a ben pekua is included.

If so, what purpose does the verbal analogy of “lamb,” “lamb,” between the firstborn donkey and the Paschal offering serve? It must be that the term “you shall redeem” does not serve to include those animals.

notes.he: ומסתברא למעוטי בן פקועה דכשחוט דמי ולא שה הוא ותפדה מרבי' בעל מום ונקבה ובן שתי שנים דשה נינהו:
notes.en: What purpose does “lamb” serve: and it is reasonable that it serves to exclude a ben pekua, which is like a slaughtered animal and is not a lamb; while “you shall redeem” includes a blemished one, a female and a two-year-old, since they are lambs.

messages.text: What is the halakha with regard to redeeming a firstborn donkey with a lamb whose parents are both sheep but it resembles another animal such as a goat?
messages.lead: § A dilemma was raised before the Sages:

notes.he: היינו שאביו איל ואמו רחל אלא שדומה למין אחר:
notes.en: With one that resembles another species: that is, its father is a ram and its mother a ewe, but it resembles another species.

messages.text: According to the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, do not raise the dilemma, as now that it is established that he holds that one may redeem with a hybrid of a goat and a sheep, with regard to a lamb that resembles a goat but is not from a hybrid, is it necessary to state that one may redeem with it?
messages.quote: And Rabbi Eliezer deems it permitted to redeem a firstborn donkey with a hybrid

notes.he: דתרי מיני הוא פרקינן דקתני במתניתין ר"א מתיר בכלאים:
notes.en: With a hybrid: which is two species, we redeem, as is taught in the mishna: Rabbi Eliezer permits with a hybrid. [Rashi writes the abbreviation ר״א, which can be read either Rabbi Eliezer or Rabbi Elazar.]

notes.he: שהרי אביו ואמו מין אחד:
notes.en: With one that resembles another species, is it necessary?: since its father and mother are of one species.

messages.text: Rather, when should you raise the dilemma? Raise it according to the opinion of the Rabbis, who hold that one may not redeem a firstborn donkey with a hybrid of a sheep and a goat. Do they hold that one does not redeem with a hybrid of a goat and a sheep, but one does redeem with a lamb that resembles another animal? Or perhaps there is no difference between them?
Come and hear a resolution from a baraita:
With regard to a cow that gave birth to a goat of sorts, one may not redeem a firstborn donkey with the goat of sorts.

notes.dh: פרה שילדה מין עז אין פודין
notes.he: דעגל הוא:
notes.en: A cow that gave birth to a goat of sorts, one may not redeem: since it is a calf.

messages.text: But it can be inferred that with regard to a ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts, one may redeem with it. Whose opinion is expressed in the baraita? If we say that it is the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, he holds that one may redeem even with a hybrid of a sheep and goat, and this ruling would be unnecessary. Rather, is it not the opinion of the Rabbis, indicating that they hold that one may redeem a firstborn donkey with a lamb that resembles another animal?

notes.he: וכ"ש בנדמה ול"ל למיתנייה:
notes.en: With a hybrid we redeem: and all the more so with one that resembles another species, and it would not need to teach it.

notes.dh: האי פרה שילדה מין עז אין פודין דאמרינן עגל הוא
notes.he: הא רחל שילדה מאיל מין עז פודין בו. וש"מ דאית ליה דפודין בנדמה מיבעיא:
notes.en: This: a cow that gave birth to a goat of sorts, one may not redeem, since we say it is a calf. But a ewe that gave birth, from a ram, to a goat of sorts, one may redeem with it. And learn from this that he holds that one may redeem with one that resembles another species. [An editor’s note in the printed text suggests a different reading here.]

messages.text: No, actually the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, and it teaches us the halakha itself that one may not redeem using the offspring in a case where a cow gave birth to a goat of sorts, i.e., where the offspring has the appearance of a goat.

notes.he: ולא משום דוקיא אתא:
notes.en: It teaches us the halakha itself: and it does not come for the inference.

notes.he: אמר לך רבי אלעזר מי קתני בבריית' רחל שילדה מין עז הא לא קתני לה בהדיא אלא למידק מיניה הכי לרבי אלעזר אע"ג דאיכא למידק הכי הא לא איצטריך לאשמועינן דכיון דבכלאים פודין כ"ש בנדמה אלא האי גופיה ברייתא גופה אצטריך לאשמועי' דפרה שילדה מין עז אין פודין אתי:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar would say to you: does the baraita teach “a ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts”? It does not teach that explicitly; one only infers it. According to Rabbi Elazar, even though one can infer this, it did not need to teach us that, since if one redeems with a hybrid, all the more so with one that resembles another species. Rather, the baraita itself comes to teach us that one may not redeem with [the offspring of] a cow that gave birth to a goat of sorts.

messages.text: This is necessary so that you do not say that the halakha should follow the appearance of the offspring itself, and therefore this offspring is a full-fledged goat and should be suitable for redeeming a firstborn donkey. Rather, follow its mother, and this offspring is treated as a calf, which is not suitable for redeeming a firstborn donkey.

notes.he: דעז מעליא הוא ופודין בו אלא זיל בתר אימיה ועגל הוא ולא איירי בנדמה אלא בהאי גופא:
notes.en: Do not say: that it is a full-fledged goat and one may redeem with it; rather, follow its mother, and it is a calf. And it is not dealing with one that resembles another species, but with this case itself.

messages.text: What is considered an animal that is a hybrid? It is a ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts and the father of the offspring is a lamb.
messages.lead: Come and hear a resolution from a baraita that Rabba bar Shmuel teaches:

messages.text: If its father is a lamb, is the offspring a hybrid? It is an animal that resembles an animal of another type.
messages.quote: and the father of the offspring is a lamb

notes.he: בתמיה. הא נדמה הוא:
notes.en: Is it a hybrid?: said in astonishment. It is one that merely resembles [another species]!

messages.text: Rather, the baraita means: What animal is similar to a hybrid, and the Rabbis rendered it tantamount to a hybrid, which is unsuitable for redeeming? It is a ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts and its father is a lamb.

notes.he: אי זה כלאים רחל וכו' הכי תריץ ליה איזהו דומה לכלאים דאע"ג דלאו כלאים הוא דשווייה רבנן לאיסוריה ככלאים היינו רחל שילדה כמין עז דהאי לאו כלאים הוא אלא נדמה ואפילו הכי אסור ככלאים:
notes.en: What is a hybrid? A ewe etc. It is explained thus: what is similar to a hybrid, which, though it is not a hybrid, the Rabbis rendered like a hybrid with regard to its prohibition? That is a ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts; this is not a hybrid but one that resembles another species, and even so it is prohibited like a hybrid.

messages.text: Now, to what halakha is this baraita referring? If it is referring to sacrificial animals, i.e., to the fact that such an animal is unfit for sacrifice as an offering, why does the baraita derive its status from that of a hybrid? From the same verse where one derives that the Torah excludes a hybrid as an offering, one can derive that it also excludes an animal that resembles an animal of another type.

notes.he: קאמר דשוייה רבנן לנדמה כי כלאים:
notes.en: To what: is it stated that the Rabbis rendered one that resembles another species like a hybrid?

notes.he: שלא יקרב לגבי מזבח ל"ל למתלייה לנדמה בכלאים כי היכי דפשיטא לן בכלאים פשיטא לן בנדמה:
notes.en: If to sacrificial animals: that it is not offered on the altar, why do I need to make the animal that resembles another species depend on a hybrid? Just as it is obvious to us with regard to a hybrid, it is obvious to us with regard to one that resembles another species.

notes.he: קאמר דאסור ככלאים אי לקדשים לזבחים מאי קמ"ל דתני רבה בר שמואל (אי לקדשים דמס') הא לא איצטריך לאשמועינן דמהיכא דמההוא קרא דממעט לכלאים מקדשים מהתם נמי אימעוט נדמה מקדשים דתניא שור או כשב וכו':
notes.en: And to what [halakha] does he say that it is prohibited like a hybrid? If to sacrificial animals, to offerings, what does Rabba bar Shmuel’s teaching tell us? That did not need to be taught to us, since from the verse that excludes a hybrid from sacrificial animals, from there one that resembles another species is also excluded from sacrificial animals, as it is taught: “A bull or a sheep” etc.

messages.text: In the verse: “When a bull, or a lamb, or a goat, is brought forth…it may be accepted as an offering…to the Lord” (Leviticus 22:27), the words “a bull, or a lamb” are interpreted as excluding a hybrid, and the words “or a goat” are interpreted as excluding an animal that resembles an animal of another type.

verse.he: שׁוֹר אוֹ־כֶשֶׂב אוֹ־עֵז כִּי יִוָּלֵד וְהָיָה שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תַּחַת אִמּוֹ וּמִיּוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי וָהָלְאָה יֵרָצֶה לְקׇרְבַּן אִשֶּׁה לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: When an ox or a sheep or a goat is born, it shall stay seven days with its mother, and from the eighth day on it shall be acceptable as an offering by fire to GOD.

messages.text: If the baraita is referring to the halakha of a firstborn and teaches that an animal that resembles an animal of another type does not have firstborn status, this is derived from another verse, as the Merciful One states: “But the firstborn of an ox” (Numbers 18:17), which indicates that there is firstborn status only if it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox, but not when the offspring resembles an animal of another type.

verse.he: אַךְ בְּכוֹר־שׁוֹר אוֹ־בְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב אוֹ־בְכוֹר עֵז לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם אֶת־דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת־חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But the firstlings of cattle, sheep, or goats may not be redeemed; they are consecrated. You shall dash their blood against the altar, and turn their fat into smoke as an offering by fire for a pleasing odor to GOD.

notes.he: לאשמועי' דלא קדוש בבכורה ככלאים פשיטא דאך בכור שור כתיב ובהדיא אימעוט:
notes.en: If to a firstborn: to teach us that, like a hybrid, it is not consecrated as a firstborn; that is obvious, since “But the firstborn of an ox” is written, and it is excluded explicitly.

notes.he: ואי משום למעוטי נדמה מבכור הא נמי מקרא נפקא דכתיב אך בכור שור עד שיהא הוא שור ובכורו שור פרט לנדמה:
notes.en: And if it is to exclude one that resembles another species from firstborn status, that too is derived from a verse, as it is written: “But the firstborn of an ox”: only if it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox, which excludes one that resembles another species.

messages.text: Rather, perhaps it is referring to the mitzva of the animal tithe and teaches that an animal that resembles an animal of another type is not tithed with the other animals. This ruling is also unnecessary, as it is derived via a verbal analogy from the word: “Under” (Leviticus 22:27), which is stated with regard to sacrificial animals, and the word: “Under” (Leviticus 27:32), which is stated in the context of animal tithe.

verse.he: וְכׇל־מַעְשַׂר בָּקָר וָצֹאן כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹר תַּחַת הַשָּׁבֶט הָעֲשִׂירִי יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: All tithes of the herd or flock—of all that passes under the shepherd’s staff, every tenth one—shall be holy to GOD.

notes.he: דכי היכי דכלאים לא מעשרין אף נדמה לא:
notes.en: If to exclude it from the tithe: that just as hybrids are not tithed, so too one that resembles another species is not.

notes.he: פשיטא תרווייהו מחד קרא נפקי תחת תחת כתיב הכא תחת השבט וכתיב בקדשים תחת אמו מה התם נדמה וכלאים לא כדממעטינן לעיל אף מעשר כלאים ונדמה לא:
notes.en: That is obvious; both derive from one verse, “under,” “under.” Here it is written: “Under the rod” (Leviticus 27:32), and with regard to sacrificial animals it is written: “Under its mother” (Leviticus 22:27). Just as there a hybrid and one that resembles another species are not [offered], as we excluded them above, so too with the tithe, a hybrid and one that resembles another species are not [tithed].

messages.text: Rather, the baraita must be referring to the lamb that is used to redeem a firstborn donkey, and it teaches that a lamb that resembles an animal of another type is unfit for use as redemption.

notes.he: דלא פרקינן ביה פטר חמור כי כלאים:
notes.en: For a firstborn donkey: that we do not redeem a firstborn donkey with it, as with a hybrid.

notes.he: ואי למעוטי ממעשר בהמה תחת תחת מקדשים גמר כתיב במעשר כל אשר יעבור תחת השבט וכתיב בקדשים תחת אמו מה התם פרט לנדמה אף במעשר נמי אלא לאו לפטר חמור איצטריך לאשמועינן דהא דתני רבה בר שמואל דאין פודין בנדמה ותפשוט מהכא:
notes.en: And if to exclude it from animal tithe, “under,” “under” is derived from sacrificial animals: it is written with regard to tithe, “whatever passes under the rod,” and it is written with regard to sacrificial animals, “under its mother”; just as there it excludes one that resembles another species, so too with tithe. Rather, is it not necessary for a firstborn donkey, to teach us, in what Rabba bar Shmuel teaches, that one may not redeem with one that resembles another species? Then resolve [the dilemma] from here.

messages.text: No, actually the baraita is referring to the halakha of animal tithe in a case where the animal that resembles an animal of another type has some characteristics of the mother.

notes.he: דאמו:
notes.en: Some characteristics: of its mother.

notes.he: לא תפשוט ולמעשר איצטריך למעוטי וכגון דיש בו מקצת סימן דומים לאמו:
notes.en: No, actually: do not resolve it from here; it was necessary to exclude it from the tithe, in a case where it has some characteristics resembling its mother.

messages.text: It was necessary for the baraita to teach that such an animal is not included in the animal tithe, lest you say that it is derived via a verbal analogy from the term: Passing, stated with regard to the animal tithe (see Leviticus 27:32), and the term: Passing, stated with regard to a firstborn animal (see Exodus 13:12), that just as an animal with some characteristics of the mother does have firstborn status (see 16b), so too, such an animal should be included in the obligation of animal tithe.

notes.he: כתיב הכא יעבור תחת השבט וכתיב בבכור והעברת פטר רחם מה בבכורה חייב כדאמרן ואם יש בו מקצת סימנין חייב אף מעשר נמי ליהוי חייב:
notes.en: “Passing,” “passing”: here it is written: “Whatever passes under the rod” (Leviticus 27:32), and with regard to the firstborn it is written: “You shall cause to pass to the Lord every one that opens the womb” (Exodus 13:12). Just as with a firstborn it is obligated, as we said, if it has some characteristics [of its mother], so too it should be obligated in the tithe.

notes.he: העברה העברה מבכור גמר כתיב במעשר כל אשר יעבור תחת השבט וכתיב בבכור והעברת כל פטר רחם מה גבי בכור אמרינן כי יש בו מקצת סימנין דומין לאמו חייב בבכורה אף במעשר נמי נימא דכי יש במקצת סימנין דליחייב במעשר:
notes.en: Lest you say: “passing,” “passing” is derived from a firstborn. It is written with regard to tithe, “whatever passes under the rod,” and it is written with regard to a firstborn, “you shall cause to pass every one that opens the womb.” Just as with regard to a firstborn we say that when it has some characteristics resembling its mother it is obligated in firstborn status, so too with tithe let us say that when it has some characteristics it is obligated in the tithe.

messages.text: Therefore, the tanna teaches us that it is derived via a verbal analogy from the word “under” that is stated with regard to sacrificial animals and the word “under” that is stated in the context of animal tithe, that an animal with some characteristics of the mother is unfit for animal tithe.

notes.he: דדין כלאים אית ליה דתחת תחת גמר מקדשים כי היכי דלמזבח לא קרב כדאמר בריש פירקין (בכורות דף ג:) מום קבוע הוא לישחט עליו במעשר נמי לא קדוש:
notes.en: It teaches us: that the halakha of a hybrid applies to it, since “under,” “under” is derived from sacrificial animals. Just as it is not offered on the altar, as is said at the beginning of our chapter (Bekhorot 3b) that it is a permanent blemish and may be slaughtered on account of it, so too it is not consecrated as tithe.

notes.dh: קא משמע לן תחת תחת משלמים גמר
notes.he: וא"ת למה לי בבכור עד שיהא הוא שור ובכורו שור נילף העברה העברה ממעשר וי"ל משום דכתיב אך לחייב מקצת סימנין דומין לאמו לכך צריך למעט נדמה בהאי קרא דנשמע מינה אמאי קאי אך ומיהו לההוא תנא דממעט לעיל נדמה מפטר חמור תרי זמני וגלי לן בקדושת דמים וה"ה לקדושת הגוף לפי טעם זה לא הוה מצי למדרש מקצת סימנים מאך ושמא נפקא ליה מקרא אחרינא:
notes.en: It teaches us that “under,” “under” is derived from peace offerings [Tosafot’s heading reads “peace offerings” where the Gemara has “sacrificial animals”]: and if you say: why do I need, with regard to a firstborn, “until it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox”? Let us derive “passing,” “passing” from the tithe! One can say: because “but” [akh] is written to obligate [an offspring with] some characteristics resembling its mother, therefore it is necessary to exclude one that resembles another species in this verse, so that we learn from it what “but” refers to. However, according to that tanna who excluded one that resembles another species above from a firstborn donkey twice, and so revealed it to us with regard to monetary sanctity, and the same applies to inherent sanctity, by this reasoning he could not have derived “some characteristics” from “but”; and perhaps he derives it from another verse.

notes.he: דתני רבה בר שמואל דלא משום דתחת תחת מקדשים גמר:
notes.en: It teaches us: in what Rabba bar Shmuel teaches, that it is not [obligated], since “under,” “under” is derived from sacrificial animals.

messages.text: The status of such a lamb with regard to redeeming a firstborn donkey may not be proven from the baraita.

notes.he: ואכתי לא ידעינן אי פודין אי לא פודין:
notes.en: And we still do not know whether one may redeem [with one that resembles another species] or may not redeem.

messages.text: What is the halakha with regard to redeeming a firstborn donkey with disqualified consecrated animals that were redeemed? It is forbidden to shear or work such animals. Does the principle of: A prohibition does not take effect where another prohibition already exists, apply here?
messages.lead: § A dilemma was raised before the Sages:

notes.he: שנפדו ויוצאין לחולין:
notes.en: Disqualified consecrated animals: that were redeemed and go out to non-sacred status.

messages.text: According to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon, you should not raise the dilemma. Since he says that it is permitted to derive benefit from a firstborn donkey, its status is non-sacred, and no forbidden status is transferred to the redemption lamb.

notes.he: פטר חמור מותר בהנאה קודם פדיון חולין הוא הפטר חמור ויכול לפדותו בה דליכא למימר איסור חל על איסור:
notes.en: Since he says: that a firstborn donkey is permitted for benefit before its redemption, the firstborn donkey is non-sacred, and he can redeem it with this [disqualified consecrated animal], since one cannot say that a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition.

notes.he: כגון בעל מום שנפדו כיון דאמר פטר חמור מותר בהנאה קודם פדייה חולין הוא שמותר בהנאה כחולין. ופרקינן בבהמה פסולי המוקדשין דכיון דמותר בהנאה אין כאן איסור חל על איסור דפסולי המוקדשין יש כאן איסור גיזה ועבידה כדאמר בפרק דלקמן תזבח ולא גיזה בשר ולא חלב דהיינו עבודה חולב:
notes.en: Disqualified consecrated animals: for example, blemished ones that were redeemed. Since he says that a firstborn donkey is permitted for benefit before its redemption, it is non-sacred, as it is permitted for benefit like non-sacred property. And one may redeem with an animal of disqualified consecrated animals, since, as it is permitted for benefit, there is no prohibition taking effect on a prohibition here; for disqualified consecrated animals carry a prohibition of shearing and of labor, as is said in the chapter below: “You may slaughter,” and not shear; “meat,” and not milk.

messages.text: When should you raise the dilemma? Raise it according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who says that it is prohibited to derive benefit from a firstborn donkey.

What is the halakha? It could be reasoned that since it is prohibited to derive benefit from the firstborn donkey, when he redeems it with a lamb, the forbidden status of the donkey must be able to be transferred to the lamb, which cannot occur in the case of a disqualified consecrated lamb, as a prohibition does not take effect where another prohibition already exists.

notes.he: פטר חמור חל על איסור דבהמת פסולי המוקדשין אית בה קדושה אפי' לאחר פדיון דאסירי בגיזה ועבודה:
notes.en: A prohibition does not take effect: the prohibition of the firstborn donkey does not take effect on the prohibition [already on the lamb], since an animal of disqualified consecrated animals retains sanctity even after its redemption, as they are prohibited in shearing and in labor.

notes.dh: אלא כי תיבעי לך אליבא דרבי יהודה וכו'
notes.he: אין איסור פטר חמור דאסור בהנאה [חל] על איסור פסולי המוקדשים דאסור בגיזה ובעבודה הילכך אין פודין:
notes.en: Rather, when should you raise the dilemma? According to Rabbi Yehuda etc.: the prohibition of a firstborn donkey, which is prohibited for benefit, does not take effect on the prohibition of disqualified consecrated animals, which are prohibited in shearing and in labor; therefore one may not redeem.

messages.text: Or perhaps it could be reasoned that since the actual prohibition against deriving benefit from the donkey is not transferred to its object of redemption, i.e., the lamb, as deriving benefit from the lamb is permitted, the act of redemption should be seen as merely an abrogation of the donkey’s forbidden status. The forbidden status is not transferred to the lamb, and consequently the principle that a prohibition does not take effect where another prohibition already exists does not apply.

notes.he: שהשה הניתן תחתיו אין בו משום קדושה:
notes.en: Since it does not seize its redemption: the lamb given in its stead has no sanctity.

notes.he: כיון דלא אלים קדושת פטר חמור למיתפס פדיונו שיהא אסור בהנאה. והאי דחייבא רחמנא למיפרקיה אפקועי איסורין בעלמא הוא כדי שיהא ניתר פטר חמור בהנאה ולא שתהא חלה קדושתו על פדיונו. הכי נמי אין איסורו חלה כלל על איסורי פסולי המוקדשים ואין [כאן] איסור חל על איסור ופודין בבהמה פסולי המוקדשין:
notes.en: Or perhaps: since the sanctity of a firstborn donkey is not strong enough to seize its redemption so that it would be prohibited for benefit, and that which the Merciful One required redeeming it is merely an abrogation of the prohibition, so that the firstborn donkey becomes permitted for benefit, and not so that its sanctity takes effect on its redemption; so too its prohibition does not take effect at all on the prohibition of disqualified consecrated animals, and there is no prohibition taking effect on a prohibition here, and one may redeem with an animal of disqualified consecrated animals.

messages.text: Is that which is written with regard to disqualified consecrated animals insignificant? The Torah states that their status is: “Like the gazelle and like the hart” (Deuteronomy 12:15), indicating that just as one may not redeem a firstborn donkey with a gazelle or a hart, so too, one may not redeem a firstborn donkey with disqualified consecrated animals.

verse.he: רַק בְּכׇל־אַוַּת נַפְשְׁךָ תִּזְבַּח ׀ וְאָכַלְתָּ בָשָׂר כְּבִרְכַּת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַן־לְךָ בְּכׇל־שְׁעָרֶיךָ הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר יֹאכְלֶנּוּ כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל׃
verse.en: But whenever you desire, you may slaughter and eat meat in any of your settlements, according to the blessing that the ETERNAL your God has granted you. The impure and the pure alike may partake of it, as of the gazelle and the deer.

notes.he: כתיב בפסולי המוקדשין דכתיב (דברים י״ב:ט״ו) רק בכל אות נפשך וגו' ובפסולי המוקדשין מדבר:
notes.en: A gazelle and a hart: is written with regard to disqualified consecrated animals, as it is written: “Notwithstanding, you may slaughter and eat meat after all the desire of your soul” (Deuteronomy 12:15), and it is speaking of disqualified consecrated animals.

notes.dh: מה צבי ואיל אין פודין וכו'
notes.he: עוד יש דרשא בפ' שני (לקמן בכורות דף טו.) מצבי ואיל דפטר להו ממתנות ואי לאו מיעוטא דקרא הוה שרי חלבו ופטר להו מאותו ואת בנו וא"ת היכי עבדינן כל הנך דרשות דפרק כל פסולי (לקמן בכורות דף לג.) אמר תלתא צבי ואיל כתיבי ומייתי כל חד למילתיה ולא דרשינן מינייהו הך דרשות כלל:
notes.en: Just as one may not redeem with a gazelle and a hart etc.: there is another exposition of “a gazelle and a hart” in the second chapter (below, Bekhorot 15a), which exempts them [disqualified consecrated animals] from the priestly gifts; and were it not for an exclusion in the verse, its fat would be permitted, and it would exempt them from [the prohibition of slaughtering] it and its offspring [on the same day]. And if you say: how do we make all these expositions, when in the chapter Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (below, Bekhorot 33a) it says that “a gazelle and a hart” is written three times, and each one is brought for its own matter, and we do not expound these expositions from them at all?

notes.he: בפסולי המוקדשין בשעריך תאכלנו הטמא והטהור יחדיו כצבי וכאיל והאי הטמא היינו בעל מום. מה צבי ואיל אין פודין בו כדתנן אין פודין לא בחיה:
notes.en: Is that which is written with regard to them insignificant: with regard to disqualified consecrated animals: “You shall eat it within your gates, the impure and the pure alike, like the gazelle and like the hart”; and this “impure” is a blemished one. Just as one may not redeem with a gazelle and a hart, as we learned: one may not redeem with an undomesticated animal.

messages.text: Now that you have arrived at this explanation,

notes.he: השתא דאתית להכי אפילו לר' שמעון נמי דשרי בהנאה אפי' הכי אין פודין דצבי ואיל כתי' בהו:
notes.en: Now that you have arrived at this: even according to Rabbi Shimon, who permits benefit, even so one may not redeem, since “a gazelle and a hart” is written with regard to them.

messages.text: according to Rabbi Shimon as well, perhaps one cannot redeem a firstborn donkey with disqualified consecrated animals, as it is written with regard to them that they are to be treated: “Like the gazelle and like the hart” (Deuteronomy 12:15). Since a gazelle and a hart cannot be used for redemption, so too, disqualified consecrated animals cannot be used for redemption.

notes.he: אע"ג דשרי פטר חמור בהנאה אין פודין אותו בפסולי המוקדשין דצבי ואיל כתיב בהו:
notes.en: According to Rabbi Shimon as well: even though he permits benefit from a firstborn donkey, one does not redeem it with disqualified consecrated animals, since “a gazelle and a hart” is written with regard to them.

messages.text: What is the halakha with regard to redeeming a firstborn donkey with an animal that was purchased with produce of the Sabbatical Year, which caused the sanctity of the produce to be transferred to the animal?
messages.lead: § A dilemma was raised before the Sages:

notes.he: בהמה שניקחה בפירות שביעית:
notes.en: With a Sabbatical animal: an animal that was purchased with produce of the Sabbatical Year.

notes.he: בבהמת שביעית בשה שקנוי מפירות שביעית:
notes.en: With a Sabbatical animal: with a lamb that was purchased with produce of the Sabbatical Year.

messages.text: With regard to redeeming a donkey that has definite firstborn status with an animal that was purchased with produce of the Sabbatical Year, you should not raise the dilemma, as one certainly may not redeem it in this manner, since the owner acquires his firstborn donkey in exchange for the animal that he gives to the priest, and this is prohibited with regard to such an animal. This is because the Merciful One states with regard to the Sabbatical Year: “The rest of the land shall be for you for consumption” (Leviticus 25:6), indicating that the produce may be used for consumption but not for commerce.

verse.he: וְהָיְתָה שַׁבַּת הָאָרֶץ לָכֶם לְאׇכְלָה לְךָ וּלְעַבְדְּךָ וְלַאֲמָתֶךָ וְלִשְׂכִירְךָ וּלְתוֹשָׁבְךָ הַגָּרִים עִמָּךְ׃
verse.en: But you may eat whatever the land during its sabbath will produce—you, your male and female slaves, the hired and bound laborers who live with you,

notes.he: פטר חמור ודאי לא תיבעי לך דכיון דבעי למיתב פדיונו לכהן לא פריק ליה דלאכלה אמר רחמנא ולא לסחורה ונמצא זה קונה חמור בפירות שביעית שאינו ראוי לאכילה:
notes.en: A definite one, you should not raise the dilemma: about a definite firstborn donkey you should not ask, since he must give its redemption to the priest, he may not redeem it [with such an animal], as the Merciful One said “for consumption,” and not for commerce; and it turns out that he acquires a donkey, which is not fit to eat, with Sabbatical produce.

notes.he: לאכלה ולא לסחורה משמע דאסור לקנות בהמה טמאה כגון פטר חמור בפירות שביעית ותימה דאפי' רבנן לא אסרי בהגוזל קמא (ב"ק קב.) משרה וכביסה אלא משום דבעינן דומיא דלאכלה שהנאתו וביעורו שוה ובהמה למלאכה הוי הנאתו וביעורו שוה:
notes.en: A definite one, you should not raise the dilemma: “for consumption, and not for commerce” implies that it is prohibited to purchase a non-kosher animal, such as a firstborn donkey, with Sabbatical produce. And this is puzzling, for even the Rabbis prohibit only soaking and laundering [with Sabbatical produce], in the first chapter of HaGozel (Bava Kamma 102a), because we require [a use] similar to “for consumption,” where its benefit and its consumption coincide; and an animal for labor is [a case] where its benefit and its consumption coincide.

notes.he: ודאי פטר חמור לא לך דאין פודין בבהמת שביעית דלאכלה אמר רחמנא והבהמה יש לה מן הפירות ולא לסחורה. דהיינו סחורה שפודה הפטר חמור בהאי שה:
notes.en: A definite firstborn donkey, you should not raise the dilemma, since one may not redeem with a Sabbatical animal, as the Merciful One said “for consumption” (and the animal has [the status] of the produce), and not for commerce; and this is commerce, that he redeems the firstborn donkey with this lamb.

messages.text: Rather, when should you raise the dilemma? Raise it in the case of a donkey with uncertain firstborn status.

notes.he: כגון שילדה אמו זכר ונקבה דאמר במתני' מפריש טלה והוא לעצמו:
notes.en: Uncertain: for example, where its mother gave birth to a male and a female, where it says in the mishna that he designates a lamb and it is his own.

notes.he: אם יכול לפדות בה ספק פטר חמור:
notes.en: When should you raise the dilemma? An uncertain one: whether he can redeem an uncertain firstborn donkey with it.

messages.text: And according to the opinion of Rabbi Shimon you should not raise the dilemma, as he does not hold that redemption is necessary in the case of a donkey with uncertain firstborn status.

notes.dh: ואליבא דרבי שמעון לא תיבעי לך
notes.he: דלדידיה לא מיתבעי לאפרושי טלה לאפקועי איסוריה אי לא יהיב ליה לכהן דהא ר"ש מתיר פטר חמור בהנאה:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Shimon you should not raise the dilemma: since according to him one need not designate a lamb to abrogate its prohibition when he does not give it to the priest, as Rabbi Shimon permits benefit from a firstborn donkey.

notes.he: ואליבא דר' שמעון דלית ליה ספק ברישא דשמעתין וכיון דלעצמו הוא למה לי לאפרושי וכו'. ואמרינן [לעיל] מתניתין ר' יהודה היא דתני כו'. ור"ש מתיר קס"ד דר' שמעון מתיר דלא צריך לאפרושי כלל הואיל וספק הוא:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Shimon, who does not hold [that anything is required for] an uncertain one, [as] at the beginning of our discussion: “and since it is for himself, why do I need to designate” etc. And we said [above]: our mishna is Rabbi Yehuda, as it teaches etc., and Rabbi Shimon permits; it was thought that Rabbi Shimon permits, since one need not designate at all, as it is uncertain.

notes.he: דמותר לפדות דהא לאו סחורה היא דבלא פדיון נמי הוה מותר:
notes.en: You should not raise the dilemma: since it is permitted to redeem, for this is not commerce, since even without redemption it would be permitted.

messages.text: When should you raise the dilemma? Raise it according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda, who holds that in such a case the owner of the donkey must designate a lamb for its redemption in order to abrogate its forbidden status, but he is not required to give it to a priest.

notes.dh: כי תבעי לך אליבא דר' יהודה
notes.he: דמצריך לאפרושי לאפקועיה איסוריה:
notes.en: When should you raise the dilemma? According to Rabbi Yehuda: who requires designating to abrogate its prohibition.

messages.text: What is the halakha? Perhaps since he designates a lamb and it is his, we call this act of redemption “for consumption,” and it is not considered commerce if he does not give it to the priest in exchange for his donkey.

notes.he: מאי כיון דמפריש טלה והוא לעצמו לאכלה קרינן ביה הואיל ולעצמו הוא:
notes.en: What is the halakha? Since he designates a lamb and it is his own, we call it “for consumption,” since it is his own.

messages.text: Or perhaps, since as long as the lamb does not abrogate the forbidden status of the firstborn donkey it is not permitted to derive benefit from the donkey, when the owner designates the lamb as the replacement of the donkey it is tantamount to engaging in commerce with it.

notes.he: או דלמא כיון דכמה דלא מפקע לאיסור בהאי שה מי שרי ליה האי פטר חמור בהנאה וכסחורה דמי שקונה הנאתו בהאי שה ואסור:
notes.en: Or perhaps, since as long as he has not abrogated the prohibition with this lamb, this firstborn donkey is not permitted to him for benefit, it is like commerce, for he acquires its benefit with this lamb, and it is prohibited.

messages.text: One may not redeem a donkey with definite firstborn status with an animal that was purchased with produce of the Sabbatical Year, but one may redeem a donkey with uncertain firstborn status with it.
messages.lead: Come and hear a resolution from that which Rav Ḥisda says:

notes.he: פטר חמור ודאי משום דבעי ליתנו לכהן והויא סחורה:
notes.en: The definite one: a definite firstborn donkey, because he must give it to the priest, and it is commerce.

notes.he: פטר חמור דהיינו סחורה:
notes.en: One may not redeem with it the definite one: a firstborn donkey, since that is commerce.

notes.he: דלא כסחורה גמורה הוא דלא הוי [אלא] ספק:
notes.en: But one may redeem with it the uncertain one: since it is not full commerce, as it is only uncertain.

messages.text: An animal that was purchased with produce of the Sabbatical Year is exempt from its offspring being counted a firstborn, but is obligated to have gifts of the priesthood taken from it. These are the gifts to which members of the priesthood are entitled when a non-sacred animal is slaughtered.

notes.he: זרוע ולחיים והקיבה:
notes.en: In the gifts: the foreleg, the jaw and the maw.

notes.he: פטורה מן הבכורה לאכלה אמר רחמנא ולא לשרפה ואלו אמורין דבכור לשרפה קיימי וחייבת במתנות בזרוע ולחיים דלאכילה קיימי קמ"ל מיהא ברייתא דרב חסדא דפודין בו את הספק:
notes.en: And Rav Ḥisda says: it is exempt from firstborn status, since the Merciful One said “for consumption,” and not for burning, and the sacrificial portions of a firstborn stand to be burned; and it is obligated in the gifts, the foreleg and the jaw, which stand to be eaten. At any rate, Rav Ḥisda’s teaching tells us that one may redeem the uncertain one with it.

messages.text: It is exempt from its offspring being counted a firstborn because the Merciful One states with regard to produce of the Sabbatical Year that it should be used “for consumption,” but not for burning, and portions of a kosher firstborn animal are burned on the altar. And it is obligated to have gifts of the priesthood taken from it, because we call this case “for consumption,” as the priest eats them.

notes.he: ואי מיחייב בבכור סלקי אימורים לגבוה:
notes.en: For burning: and if it were obligated as a firstborn, its sacrificial portions would go up to the Most High [i.e., be burned on the altar].

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection from a mishna (Shevi’it 9:9):

One who eats from dough of produce of the Sabbatical Year before its ḥalla, i.e., the portion of the dough given to the priests, has been separated, is liable to receive the punishment of death at the hand of Heaven, just like one who consumes any dough before ḥalla is separated.

notes.he: חלה טמאה אין לה תקנה אלא שריפה דהאוכל תרומה טמאה חייב מיתה:
notes.en: Impure ḥalla has no remedy except burning, since one who eats impure teruma is liable to death.

notes.dh: עד שלא הורמה החלה חייב מיתה
notes.he: דכתיב ולא תשא עליו חטא וגו':
notes.en: Before its ḥalla was separated, is liable to death: as it is written: “And they shall not bear sin for it” etc.

messages.text: But according to the opinion of Rav Ḥisda, why is dough of produce of the Sabbatical Year subject to the obligation of separating ḥalla? It should not be subject to this mitzva, since if the dough becomes ritually impure after being separated as ḥalla, it is subject to burning, and the Merciful One states: “For consumption,” but not for burning. This is similar to Rav Ḥisda’s claim that a firstborn animal that was purchased with produce of the Sabbatical Year is not subject to the obligations of firstborn status.
messages.quote: exempt from its offspring being counted a firstborn

notes.he: מיחייב עיסת שביעית בשביעית בחלה:
notes.en: And why: is dough of Sabbatical produce obligated in ḥalla in the Sabbatical Year?

notes.he: ואע"ג דיכול להפריש מעיסה אחרת שאינה של שביעית על זאת ומקיף שתיהן מ"מ הך לאו בת חלה היא ולא מצי לאפרושי מגופה הוי כמו מן החיוב על הפטור:
notes.en: Since if it became impure etc.: and even though he could separate [ḥalla] for this dough from another dough that is not of the Sabbatical Year, joining the two, nevertheless this one is not subject to ḥalla and he cannot separate from it itself; it is like [separating] from the obligated for the exempt.

notes.he: חייב מיתה כיון דאילו מיטמיא החלה בשרפה קיימא ולאכלה אמר רחמנא ולא לשרפה והא חלה לא ליחייב עלה כיון דיש בה דין שרפה כי היכי דפטרת לה מן הבכורה הואיל ואימורין לשרפה קיימי:
notes.en: And why is he liable to death? Since if the ḥalla became impure it stands to be burned, and the Merciful One said “for consumption,” and not for burning, one should not be liable for ḥalla, since it has a law of burning, just as you exempted it from firstborn status because the sacrificial portions stand to be burned.

messages.text: Here, with regard to ḥalla, it is different, as it is written: “Of the first of your dough you shall give to the Lord a portion for a gift throughout your generations” (Numbers 15:21), which indicates that all dough, including that of produce of the Sabbatical Year, is subject to the mitzva of ḥalla.

verse.en: You shall make a gift to GOD from the first yield of your baking, throughout the ages.

notes.he: כתיב בחלה משמע אפי' בשביעית וכתיב (במדבר טו) מראשית עריסותיכם וגו':
notes.en: “Throughout your generations”: is written with regard to ḥalla, implying even in the Sabbatical Year; and it is written: “Of the first of your dough” etc. (Numbers 15).

notes.he: הא לא קשיא דאמאי חייב מיתה בשביעית דכתיב גבי חלה לדורותיכם דכתיב תתנו לה' תרומה לדורותיכם. דלעולם נוהגת איסורה אפילו בשביעית:
notes.en: This is not difficult, why he is liable to death in the Sabbatical Year: because it is written with regard to ḥalla “throughout your generations,” as it is written: “You shall give to the Lord a gift throughout your generations”: its prohibition always applies, even in the Sabbatical Year.

messages.text: From where is it derived that one who consumes dough of produce of the Sabbatical Year before its ḥalla was separated is liable to receive the punishment of death at the hand of Heaven? It is derived from a verse, as it is stated: “Throughout your generations,” which indicates the inclusion of Sabbatical Years as well.

notes.he: דטעמא משום דלדורותיכם כתיב בהו:
notes.en: This is also taught: that the reason is because “throughout your generations” is written with regard to it.

messages.text: By contrast, this formulation is not used with regard to a firstborn animal. Therefore, since portions of a kosher firstborn animal are burned on the altar, an animal that was purchased with produce of the Sabbatical Year is exempt from its offspring being counted a firstborn.

And let Rav Ḥisda derive from the halakha of ḥalla that such an animal is subject to its offspring being counted a firstborn, and that the interpretation of: “For consumption” but not for burning, is not applied.

notes.he: דלא אמר לאכלה ולא לשריפה ותתחייב בהמת שביעית בבכורה:
notes.en: And let him derive from it: that [the verse] does not say “for consumption” and not for burning, and a Sabbatical animal would be obligated in firstborn status.

notes.he: ולגמר מינה מחלה לבכורה שתהא נמי חייבת בבכורה:
notes.en: And let him derive from it: from ḥalla to firstborn status, that it too should be obligated in firstborn status.

messages.text: There, with regard to ḥalla, the primary purpose of the dough is for consumption, and it is burned only if it becomes impure. Here, with regard to a firstborn animal, the primary purpose of the portions that are consumed on the altar is for burning.

notes.he: גבי חלה עיקר הפרשתה לאכילה דאינה בשריפה אא"כ נטמאת:
notes.en: There: with regard to ḥalla, the primary purpose of its separation is for eating, since it is burned only if it became impure.

notes.dh: הכא עיקר לשריפה הקשה ר"ת נילף מעומר דעיקרו לשריפה
notes.he: ואמר פ' כל קרבנות (מנחות ד' פד.) שומרי ספיחין בשביעית היו נוטלין שכרן מתרומת הלשכה ופריך היכי מייתי עומר מפירות שביעית לאכלה אמר רחמנא ולא לשריפה ואיכא קומץ שקרב לגבי מזבח שאני התם דאמר קרא לדורותיכם י"ל לא ילפינן בכור מעומר דאיכא פירכי טובא מה לעומר שכן קרבן צבור ודוחה שבת וטומאה ועוד א"א לקיים עומר בשביעית אלא בפירות שביעית דבעינן כרמל אבל בכור וחלה מתקיים בשנה שביעית בבהמות אחרות ובפירות אחרים:
notes.en: Here the primary purpose is for burning: Rabbeinu Tam asked: let us derive from the omer, whose primary purpose is for burning. For it says in the chapter Kol Korbanot (Menaḥot 84a): the guards of the aftergrowth in the Sabbatical Year would take their wages from the collection of the Temple chamber; and it asks: how does one bring the omer from Sabbatical produce? The Merciful One said “for consumption,” and not for burning, and there is the handful that is offered on the altar! [And it answers:] There it is different, as the verse states: “Throughout your generations.” One can say: we do not derive a firstborn from the omer, as there are many refutations: what is notable about the omer is that it is a communal offering and overrides Shabbat and impurity. And furthermore, it is impossible to fulfill the omer in the Sabbatical Year except with Sabbatical produce, since we require fresh grain; but firstborn status and ḥalla can be fulfilled in the Sabbatical Year with other animals and other produce.

notes.he: לא דמי התם נמי משום הכי חייב עלה מיתה משום דעיקר חלה לאכילה קאי לכהן ולא לטמאה לשרפה:
notes.en: It is not similar; there, it is for this reason that he is liable to death for it: because the primary purpose of ḥalla is to be eaten by the priest, and not to become impure and be burned.

notes.he: גבי בכור עיקר אימורין לשרפה קיימי ולא לאכילה הלכך פטור מן הבכורה דלאכלה אמר רחמנא ולא לשרפה:
notes.en: Here: with regard to a firstborn, the primary purpose of the sacrificial portions is for burning and not for eating; therefore it is exempt from firstborn status, as the Merciful One said “for consumption,” and not for burning.

messages.caption: With what may a firstborn donkey be redeemed? The mishna and the dilemmas of 12a–b at a glance.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: If the owner gave the firstborn donkey itself to a priest, the priest may keep it only after he designates a lamb in its stead for redemption. This language indicates that there is concern lest the priest will be negligent in redeeming it. We learn in the mishna that which the Sages taught explicitly in a baraita:
messages.quote: If one gave the firstborn donkey to a priest, the priest may not keep it

notes.he: אפי' שעה אחת:
notes.en: To keep it: even for one moment.

notes.he: במתניתי' נמי להא ברייתא דת"ר משום דעיקר היא:
notes.en: We learn it: in our mishna as well, this baraita that the Sages taught, because it [the mishna] is primary.

messages.text: In the case of an Israelite who had a firstborn donkey in his house and the priest said to him: Give it to me and I will redeem it, he may not give the donkey to the priest unless the priest redeems it in his presence.

notes.he: הכהן בפניו:
notes.en: Unless he redeemed it: unless the priest redeemed it in his presence.

messages.text: That is to say that priests are suspect with regard to using firstborn donkeys without redemption.

notes.he: שעובדין בהן בלא פדיון:
notes.en: Are suspect: that they work with them without redemption.

notes.he: מדקאמר אא"כ פדאו בפניו ש"מ דנחשדו הכהנים על פיטרי חמורים שלא יהו פודין אותן:
notes.en: That is to say: since it says “unless he redeemed it in his presence,” learn from it that priests are suspect with regard to firstborn donkeys, that they will not redeem them.

messages.text: Isn’t it obvious? That is exactly what the baraita states.
messages.quote: priests are suspect with regard to using firstborn donkeys

notes.he: דודאי מהכא שמעינן לה:
notes.en: Obvious: since we certainly learn it from here.

notes.he: דבברייתא חזינן בפירוש דנחשדו ומאי קמ"ל רב נחמן:
notes.en: Obvious: since in the baraita we see explicitly that they are suspect; so what does Rav Naḥman teach us?

messages.text: Rav Naḥman’s statement is necessary lest you say that this statement of the baraita applies only in a case where we have a presumption that it occasionally happens that this priest uses a firstborn donkey without redeeming it first, but in the case of an ordinary priest, there is no concern for this.

notes.he: דלא יתננו היכא דמוחזק לן ביה דמיקרי חשוד שראינוהו שנחשד בדבר. ל"א דמיקרי דחזינן ליה דאיתרמי ועבד עבודה בפטר חמור קודם פדיון:
notes.en: Lest you say this applies: that he should not give it to him [only] where we have a presumption that he happens to be suspect, that we have seen him suspected in the matter. Another version: that it happens, that we saw him chance to work with a firstborn donkey before its redemption.

notes.he: אי לאו דרב נחמן הוה אמינא הני מילי דלא יתנו לו אא"כ פדאו בפניו היכא דמחזק לן בההוא דלא הוי חכם כ"כ ומיקרי ועביד ביה עבודה קודם שיפדנו:
notes.en: Lest you say: were it not for Rav Naḥman, I would have said that this, that one should not give it to him unless he redeemed it in his presence, applies only where we have a presumption about that one, that he is not so learned and it happens that he does work with it before he redeems it.

notes.he: היכא דלא מוחזק לן אימא אין צריך לפדותו בפניו דלא נחשדו קמ"ל דכולן נחשדו:
notes.en: But in an ordinary case: where we have no such presumption, I would say he need not redeem it in his presence, since they are not suspect. It teaches us that all of them are suspect.

messages.text: Therefore, Rav Naḥman teaches us that this concern is relevant to every priest, as a priest is suspected of granting himself permission to use the firstborn donkey without first redeeming it with a lamb, as in any case the lamb will remain his.

notes.he: דקסבר כיון דשה שיפריש תחתיו יהא שלי למה לי לפדותו:
notes.en: That he grants himself permission in it: since he reasons: since the lamb I would designate in its stead would be mine, why do I need to redeem it?

notes.he: משום דמורו ביה היתירא דאמר מה צורך לי לפדותי והלא כשאפדנו יהיה השה שלי ועכשיו הוא שלי ולא משגח לפדותו הלכך לא יתננו לו אא"כ פדאו בפניו:
notes.en: Because they grant themselves permission in it, saying: what need is there for me to redeem it? When I redeem it, the lamb will be mine, and now it is mine; and he does not bother to redeem it. Therefore one should not give it to him unless he redeemed it in his presence.

messages.text: Mishna
In the case of one who designates a lamb for the redemption of a firstborn donkey and the lamb dies,

The owner bears financial responsibility and must give the priest another lamb in its place. This is like the case of the five sela for redemption of a firstborn son, where if the money is lost before one gives it to the priest, he must give the priest another five sela.

notes.dh: מתני' כחמש סלעים של פדיון הבן
notes.he: דאמר בפ' יש בכור לנחלה (לקמן בכורות דף נא.) דחייב באחריותו:
notes.en: Mishna. Like the five sela of the redemption of a son: as is said in the chapter Yesh Bekhor LaNaḥala (below, Bekhorot 51a), that he bears responsibility for it.

notes.he: קודם שבא ליד כהן חייב ישראל באחריותו ליתן לו פדיון אחר כחמש סלעים של בן. כדתנן בפרק יש בכור לנחלה המפריש פדיון בנו ואבד חייב באחריות שנאמר אך פדה תפדה:
notes.en: One who designates the redemption of a firstborn donkey and it died: before it came into the priest’s hand, the Israelite bears responsibility for it, to give him another redemption, like the five sela of a son, as we learned in the chapter Yesh Bekhor LaNaḥala: one who designates the redemption of his son and it was lost bears responsibility for it, as it is stated: “Yet you shall surely redeem.”

messages.text: The owner does not bear financial responsibility. This is like the case of money designated for redemption of second-tithe produce, where once the owner designates the money for redemption, the produce is desanctified.

notes.he: דאם אבדו אינו חייב באחריותו כרבנן:
notes.en: Like the redemption of second tithe: that if it was lost, he does not bear responsibility for it, according to the Rabbis.

notes.he: וחכ"א אין חייב באחריותו כפדיון מעשר שני מה מעשר שני אם אבד פדיונו אין חייב באחריותו דשלו הוא אלא שצריך להעלותו ולאוכלו בירושלים בשיש לו מעלה ואם לאו פטור אף פדיון בכור אין חייב באחריותו העיד ר' יהושע וכולה כחכמים:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: he does not bear responsibility for it, like the redemption of second tithe: just as with second tithe, if its redemption was lost he does not bear responsibility for it, since it is his, except that he must bring it up and eat it in Jerusalem when he has [the means] to bring it up, and if not he is exempt; so too with the redemption of a firstborn [donkey], he does not bear responsibility for it. Rabbi Yehoshua testified, and it is all in accordance with the Rabbis.

messages.text: that the priest has nothing here, i.e., in such a case, as the firstborn donkey has already been redeemed, and the owner no longer bears financial responsibility for the dead lamb, in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis.
messages.lead: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Tzadok testified about a lamb designated for redemption of a firstborn donkey that died,

messages.text: If after the lamb was designated, the firstborn donkey died,

notes.he: לאחר שהפריש הפדיון ועדיין לא נתנו לכהן:
notes.en: The firstborn donkey died: after he designated its redemption and had not yet given it to the priest.

notes.he: קודם שבא טלה ליד כהן:
notes.en: The firstborn donkey died: before the lamb came into the priest’s hand.

messages.text: The donkey must be buried, and the owner is permitted to derive benefit from the lamb.

notes.he: הואיל והוא חייב באחריו' הטלה כמאן דלא אפרשיה דמי ומותר לישראל בהנאתו של טלה כמי שלא הפרישו:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: It must be buried: since he bears responsibility for the lamb, it is as though he had not designated it, and the Israelite is permitted to benefit from the lamb as one who had not designated it.

notes.he: דאסור בהנאה כמתחילה:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: It must be buried: since it is prohibited for benefit, as at first.

notes.he: ישראל בהנאה של טלה:
notes.en: And it is permitted: the Israelite is permitted to benefit from the lamb.

messages.text: It does not need to be buried, and the lamb is given to the priest.

notes.he: דמעידנא דאפרשיה לטלה קם ליה ברשות כהן ופטר חמור פדוי:
notes.en: It does not need to be buried: since from the moment he designated the lamb it stands in the priest’s possession, and the firstborn donkey is redeemed.

notes.he: ומותר בהנאת עורו ונבילתו:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: It does not need to be buried: and its hide and carcass are permitted for benefit.

notes.he: דמעידנא דאפרשיה ברשותיה דכהן קאי:
notes.en: And the lamb goes to the priest: since from the time he designated it, it stands in the priest’s possession.

messages.text: Gemara

What is the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who holds that the owner bears financial responsibility for the lamb if it is designated and dies before the priest receives it? As it is written: “Yet you shall redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of non-kosher animals you shall redeem” (Numbers 18:15).

verse.he: כׇּל־פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לְכׇל־בָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר־יַקְרִיבוּ לַיהֹוָה בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה יִהְיֶה־לָּךְ אַךְ ׀ פָּדֹה תִפְדֶּה אֵת בְּכוֹר הָאָדָם וְאֵת בְּכוֹר־הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה תִּפְדֶּה׃
verse.en: The first [male] issue of the womb of every being, human or animal, that is offered to GOD, shall be yours; but you shall have the first-born of human beings redeemed, and you shall also have the firstling of impure animals redeemed.

notes.he: אם הפריש פדיונו ואבד:
notes.en: Gemara. Bears responsibility for it: if he designated its redemption and it was lost.

messages.text: It is derived from the comparison between the two cases that just as with regard to redeeming a woman’s firstborn son, the father bears financial responsibility to compensate for the five sela in the event of their loss, so too, with regard to redeeming a firstborn non-kosher animal, the owner bears financial responsibility to compensate the priest in the event of their loss.

@Rav Yosef If they are compared, then just as deriving benefit from a woman’s firstborn son is permitted if he has not yet been redeemed, so too, deriving benefit from the firstborn of a non-kosher animal should be permitted prior to redemption, including shearing and working it.
messages.quote: Yet you shall redeem the firstborn of man

notes.he: קודם פדיונו:
notes.en: Is permitted for benefit: before its redemption.

notes.he: הואיל ומקיש לבכור אדם לקיש נמי לכולה מילתא. ולימא אי מה בכור אדם מותר בהנאת מלאכתו אף בכור בהמה טמאה נמי:
notes.en: Abaye said to him: since he compares it to a firstborn person, let him compare it in every matter as well, and say: if so, just as with a firstborn person the benefit of his labor is permitted, so too with the firstborn of a non-kosher animal.

messages.text: And if you would say that indeed Rabbi Eliezer does permit deriving benefit from a firstborn donkey, that is difficult: But didn’t we learn in the mishna that if after the lamb was designated the firstborn donkey died, Rabbi Eliezer says: It must be buried? Now, what is the reason that it must be buried? Is it not because deriving benefit from it is prohibited?
No, it must be buried like a woman’s firstborn son. There is a mitzva to bury a woman’s firstborn son if he dies, and due to the comparison of the verse, the same applies to a firstborn donkey.

notes.he: לא משום דאסור בהנאה אלא משום דאיתקש לבכור אדם וסתם בכור אדם ניתן לקבורה:
notes.en: It must be buried like a firstborn person: not because it is prohibited for benefit, but because it is compared to a firstborn person, and an ordinary firstborn person is given to burial.

notes.dh: וכי תימא הכי נמי והתנן מת וכו'
notes.he: לא לעולם מותר נמי בהנאה מאי יקבר דקאמר לאו משום דאסור בהנאה אלא הואיל ומקישו לבכור אדם יקבר נמי כבכור אדם:
notes.en: And if you would say: indeed. But didn’t we learn: it died etc.? No, actually it is permitted for benefit as well; and what is meant by “it must be buried”? Not because it is prohibited for benefit, but since he compares it to a firstborn person, it must also be buried like a firstborn person.

messages.text: But according to this answer, does a person who died require burial only if he is a firstborn son, while an ordinary person who is not a firstborn does not require burial? That is certainly not correct. Therefore, no such distinction should exist with regard to a donkey either.

notes.he: אלא מעתה בכור אדם הוא דבעי קבורה כלומר אי משום הכי אמר יקבר דלא אסור בהנאה הוא אלא דבעי קבורה לימא יקבר כאדם אלא מדאמר יקבר ש"מ דאסור בהנאה:
notes.en: But if so, is it a firstborn person who requires burial? That is, if for this reason he said “it must be buried,” not that it is prohibited for benefit but that it requires burial, let him say “it must be buried like a person.” Rather, since he said “it must be buried,” learn from it that it is prohibited for benefit.

messages.text: And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer clearly holds that deriving benefit from a firstborn donkey prior to redemption is forbidden, as it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Eliezer concedes with regard to an Israelite who has a donkey in his house whose status as a firstborn is uncertain, that he designates a lamb for it and the lamb is his.

notes.he: אע"ג דבודאי פטר חמור ס"ל דכל כמה דלא מטי פטר חמור ליד כהן לא מיפריק מודה הוא בספק שא"צ לתת פדיון לכהן אלא מפריש כו'. ומדמצריך לאפרושי טלה לאפקועי איסוריה מכלל דס"ל פטר חמור אסור בהנאה:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer concedes: although with a definite firstborn donkey he holds that as long as [its redemption] has not reached the priest’s hand it is not redeemed, he concedes with an uncertain one that he need not give the redemption to the priest, but designates etc. And since he requires designating a lamb to abrogate its prohibition, by inference he holds that a firstborn donkey is prohibited for benefit.

notes.he: שמפריש עליו טלה והוא שלו אלמא דאי לא מפריש אסור בהנאה וכ"ש פטר חמור ודאי. ומדלא אקשי להנאה לא תקיש נמי לאחריות:
notes.en: And furthermore, it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer concedes that one designates a lamb for it, and it is his. Evidently, if he does not designate, it is prohibited for benefit, and all the more so a definite firstborn donkey. And since he did not compare it with regard to benefit, he should not compare it with regard to responsibility either.

messages.text: Designating a lamb in this case is necessary only to remove the prohibition against deriving benefit from the donkey.

Although the verse compares the status of a firstborn donkey to that of a woman’s firstborn son, this is only with regard to bearing financial responsibility for the lamb, but not with regard to deriving benefit from the donkey. This is because the verse states: “Yet you shall redeem [pado tifde] the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of non-kosher animals you shall redeem.” The double verb “pado tifde” indicates that I have compared it with regard to redemption, but not with regard to another matter.

verse.he: כׇּל־פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לְכׇל־בָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר־יַקְרִיבוּ לַיהֹוָה בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה יִהְיֶה־לָּךְ אַךְ ׀ פָּדֹה תִפְדֶּה אֵת בְּכוֹר הָאָדָם וְאֵת בְּכוֹר־הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה תִּפְדֶּה׃
verse.en: The first [male] issue of the womb of every being, human or animal, that is offered to GOD, shall be yours; but you shall have the first-born of human beings redeemed, and you shall also have the firstling of impure animals redeemed.

notes.he: בכור בהמה טמאה לבכור אדם שיתחייב באחריות פדיונו ולא לדבר אחר להנאה:
notes.en: I compared it with regard to redemption: [I compared] the firstborn of a non-kosher animal to a firstborn person, that he bears responsibility for its redemption, and not with regard to another matter, for benefit.

notes.he: לעולם לפדיה לאחריות אקשינן ליה ולא להנאה וגופיה קא דשמעינן לה דכתיב אך פדה תפדה לפדייה הקשתיו לבכור אדם ולא לדבר אחר להנאה:
notes.en: Rava says: actually, we compare it with regard to redemption, for responsibility, and not for benefit; and we learn this from the verse itself, as it is written: “Yet you shall surely redeem”: I compared it to a firstborn person with regard to redemption, and not with regard to another matter, for benefit.

messages.text: § We learned in a baraita elsewhere:

Valuations are determined based on the time of the vow. Therefore, if one vowed to consecrate the valuation of an infant who is less than one month old, he is not obligated to give any money even after the infant is one month old, as an infant less than one month old has no valuation.

notes.he: שאם היה מבן חדש עד חמש שנים בשעת שאמר ערכי עלי והמתין שלא נתנו עד שיהא בן שש שיש לו ערך אחר כדכתיב בפרשת ערכין (ויקרא כז) אפי' הכי לא יהיב אלא כשעה שהעריך:
