notes.en: Valuations at their time: that if at the time he said “My valuation is upon me” he was from one month to five years old, and he waited and did not give it until he was six, when he has a different valuation, as is written in the passage of valuations (Leviticus 27), even so he gives only according to the time at which he made the valuation.

messages.text: And with regard to redeeming a woman’s firstborn son, one must give the required sum to the priest after the infant is thirty days old, as it is stated: “And their redemption money, from a month old shall you redeem them” (Numbers 18:16). With regard to redeeming a firstborn donkey, it must be performed immediately.

verse.he: וּפְדוּיָו מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּה בְּעֶרְכְּךָ כֶּסֶף חֲמֵשֶׁת שְׁקָלִים בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה הוּא׃
verse.en: Take as their redemption price, from the age of one month up, the money equivalent of five shekels by the sanctuary weight, which is twenty gerahs.

notes.he: כדכתיב (במדבר י״ח:ט״ו-ט״ז) ופדויו מבן חדש וגו':
notes.en: After thirty: as it is written: “And their redemption money, from a month old” etc. (Numbers 18:15–16).

notes.he: שאם העריך קטן ואח"כ הגדיל אין חייב ליתן אלא כשעה שהעריכו ופדיון הבן אינו חייב ליתנו אלא אחר שלשים דעד שלשים חיישינן שלא יהא נפל:
notes.en: Valuations at their time: that if he valuated a minor and afterward the minor grew up, he need give only according to the time at which he valuated him. And the redemption of a son he is obligated to give only after thirty [days], since until thirty we are concerned that he may be a non-viable newborn.

messages.text: And must redeeming a firstborn donkey be performed immediately? But one can raise a contradiction from another baraita:
messages.quote: With regard to redeeming a firstborn donkey, it must be performed immediately

notes.he: בתמיה:
notes.en: And redemption of a firstborn donkey is immediate?: said in astonishment.

notes.dh: ופטר חמור לאלתר פודין אותו אפי' בתוך שלשים
notes.he: ורמינהי אין בערכין דפחות מחודש אין לו ערך. ואין נזירות פחות מל' דכתיב קדוש יהיה בגימטריא ל' ופדיון הבן ופדיון פטר חמור אין פחות משלשים יום:
notes.en: And a firstborn donkey immediately: one redeems it even within thirty [days]. And one raises a contradiction: there are no valuations [for less than thirty days], since one less than a month old has no valuation; and there is no naziriteship of less than thirty [days], as it is written: “He shall be [yihyeh] holy,” which in gematria is thirty; and the redemption of a son and the redemption of a firstborn donkey [do] not [apply] in less than thirty days.

messages.text: The halakhot of valuations, and of redemption of a woman’s firstborn son, and of nazirite vows, and of a firstborn donkey, do not apply to less than thirty days. In other words, the halakhot of valuations, of the redemption of a woman’s firstborn son, and of a firstborn donkey do not apply to a person or animal that is less than thirty days old, and a term of naziriteship is a minimum of thirty days.

notes.he: אינו נערך כדכתיב בפרשה:
notes.en: There are no valuations for less than thirty days: such a one is not valuated, as is written in the passage.

notes.he: סתם נזירות שלשים יום כדכתיב (במדבר ו׳:ה׳) קודש יהיה יהיה בגימטריא שלשים הוו:
notes.en: And of naziriteship: an unspecified naziriteship is thirty days, as it is written: “He shall be [yihyeh] holy” (Numbers 6:5), and yihyeh in gematria is thirty.

messages.text: But one may add to this amount forever. Meaning, the halakhot of valuations apply to a person of any age beyond thirty days, the redemption of a woman’s firstborn son and of a firstborn donkey apply even if the firstborn in question is already several years old, and one can vow to be a nazirite for any length of time beyond thirty days.

notes.he: שיש ערך לכל זמן שהוא עומד בו כדכתיב בפרשה וכן נזיר נודר בנזיר ארבעה וחמשה שנים ואם המתין מפדיון בנו ומפדיון פטר חמורו כמה שנים עדיין יכול לפדותו ואינו נותן יותר:
notes.en: And one may add: since there is a valuation for every age at which he stands, as is written in the passage; and likewise a nazirite may vow a naziriteship of four or five years; and if he waited several years with the redemption of his son or the redemption of his firstborn donkey, he can still redeem it, and he does not give more.

notes.he: דלאחר ל' ולמעלה יכול להעריכו עד עולם ויש בו תוספת ערך כשהוא גדול:
notes.en: And one may add forever: since from thirty [days] and up one can valuate him forever, and there is an increase in valuation when he is older.

notes.he: דאם רצה להוסיף על ל' כמה שירצה עד עולם שרי. ופדיון הבן ופטר חמור משלשים ולמעלה יכול לפדותן עד עולם. והיינו ומוסיפין עלהן. אבל בפדיונן אין תוספת דמים דכמה שיתן כשהן מן שלשים יום כך יתן בכל זמן שרוצה לפדותן. אלמא דאין פודין פטר חמור פחות משלשים יום:
notes.en: And in naziriteship: that if he wants to add to thirty as much as he wishes, forever, it is permitted. And the redemption of a son and of a firstborn donkey: from thirty and up he can redeem them forever; and that is “and one may add to them.” But in their redemption there is no addition of value: as much as he would give when they are thirty days old, so he gives at any time he wishes to redeem them. Evidently one does not redeem a firstborn donkey in less than thirty days.

messages.text: This baraita indicates that a firstborn donkey is not redeemed immediately, but only after thirty days.

When the first baraita states that a firstborn donkey must be redeemed immediately, it means to say that if one redeemed it immediately, it is redeemed, although it should be redeemed only after thirty days ab initio.

notes.he: הא דקתני לעיל פדיון פטר חמור לאלתר שאם פדאו לאלתר [פדוי] אבל עיקר מצות פדייה לא מקיים:
notes.en: To say that if he redeemed it, it is redeemed: that which was taught above, “redemption of a firstborn donkey is immediate,” means that if he redeemed it immediately it is [redeemed], but he does not fulfill the primary mitzva of redemption.

notes.he: אמר רב נחמן אמר רב מאי לאלתר דקאמר לומר שאם פדאו לאלתר פטור דאיעבד:
notes.en: Rav Naḥman said that Rav said: what is meant by “immediately” that it states? To say that if he redeemed it immediately, it is exempt after the fact. [Rabbeinu Gershom reads “Rav Naḥman said that Rav said”; the daf reads “Rav Naḥman says.”]

messages.text: By inference, in the case of a woman’s firstborn son, where the first baraita states that he is redeemed after thirty days, if one redeemed him prior to that time, is he not redeemed? But wasn’t it stated: In the case of one who redeems his son within thirty days of birth,

notes.he: מדאוקמת ליה בדיעבד וקתני הבן אחר שלשים מכלל דאם פדאו בתוך שלשים אינו פדוי:
notes.en: By inference, his son: since you established it as after the fact, and it teaches that a son is after thirty, by inference if he redeemed him within thirty he is not redeemed.

messages.text: His son is redeemed.

notes.he: בפ' יש בכור לנחלה (לקמן בכורות דף מט.):
notes.en: But wasn’t it stated: in the chapter Yesh Bekhor LaNaḥala (below, Bekhorot 49a).

messages.text: Wasn’t it stated with regard to that matter:

Everyone agrees that if one says within thirty days of his son’s birth that he is redeeming him from now, his son is not redeemed. Such a redemption would be effective only if he gave the money on condition that the redemption will take effect after his son turns thirty days old.

notes.he: היכא דאמר ליה מעכשיו יחול פדיון זה אינו פדוי כי פליגי היכא דאמר עכשיו אני נותן מעות והפדיון לא יחול עד לאחר שלשים יום:
notes.en: Everyone agrees, “from now”: where he said to him: Let this redemption take effect from now, he is not redeemed. Where they disagree is where he said: I am giving the money now, and the redemption will not take effect until after thirty days.

notes.dh: לאו איתמר עלה אמר רבא דכ"ע מעכשיו אינו פדוי
notes.he: לשון זה אינו לקמן פ' יש בכור (בכורות דף מט. ע"ש):
notes.en: Wasn’t it stated with regard to that: Rava says: Everyone agrees that with “from now” he is not redeemed: this wording is not found below, in the chapter Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 49a; see there).

notes.he: דרבנן דברייתא דאין בערכין סברי דאם פדאו קודם אינו פדוי דיעבד. והא איתמר כו' א"כ מאי בינייהו וליכא לתרוצי כדקאמרת לומר שאם פדאו פדוי לעולם כדתרצינן ודקא קשיא והא איתמר הפודה כו' הא איתמר עלה דההוא דכולי עלמא מעכשיו כלומר אמר בתוך שלשים הרי זה פדיונו שיהא פדוי מעכשיו קודם שלשים אין בנו פדוי אפי' דיעבד משום דכי אמר מעכשיו דמי כמאן דהשתא נמי ליהוי מצותיה ולא הוה עד שלשים אלמא דרבנן סברי אם פדאו אינו פדוי:
notes.en: By inference: the Rabbis of the baraita that says “there are no valuations” hold that if he redeemed [his son] before [thirty days], he is not redeemed, even after the fact. But wasn’t it stated etc.? If so, what is the difference between them? And one cannot answer as you said, “to say that if he redeemed it, it is redeemed,” for all cases, as we answered. And as for what is difficult, “but wasn’t it stated: one who redeems” etc.: wasn’t it stated with regard to that: everyone agrees that with “from now,” that is, where he said within thirty [days], “This is his redemption, that he be redeemed from now,” before thirty, his son is not redeemed even after the fact, because when he says “from now” it is as if he wants the mitzva to be now as well, and it is not [its time] until thirty. Evidently the Rabbis hold that if he redeemed him, he is not redeemed.

messages.text: Continues on 13a: Rav Sheshet offers another way to reconcile the two baraitot.
